rulers.name: Itzcoatl

rulers.name: Tizoc

rulers.name: Cuauhtemoc

region.text: the Basin of Mexico: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan and the Tepanec lands carved up between them

ledger.note: 1428: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan defeat Azcapotzalco and found the Triple Alliance. 'In 1427, Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan, and Huexotzinco went to war against Azcapotzalco, emerging victorious in 1428.' Infobox 'Alliance founded: 1428'; the Tepanec War page adds that 'in 1430' the three remaining cities formed the treaty 'now known as the Triple Alliance' (Huexotzinco withdrew). The year is the pages'; the region is Cliopatria's 1429 shape.

region.text: the Mexica city, senior partner

ledger.note: 1428: Tenochtitlan becomes the senior partner of the alliance. Infobox 'Formation of the Aztec Empire: 1428'.

region.text: Tetzcoco and its Acolhua kingdoms

ledger.note: 1428: Texcoco joins the alliance as the second partner. 'founded in 1428 when the rulers of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan formed an alliance'; the Texcoco page says it received two-fifths of the tribute, Tlacopan one-fifth.

region.text: Tlacopan (Tacuba), the dissident Tepanec city

ledger.note: 1428: Tlacopan, the dissident Tepanec city that backed the Mexica, joins as junior partner. 'A tribute was divided so that two kings of the alliance would go to Tenochtitlan and Texcoco and one would go to Tlacopan.' The region is the place's own, read as a 12 km disc.

region.text: the Tepanec lands around Azcapotzalco

ledger.note: 1428: the Tepanec lands are divided among the three victors. 'The Tepanec lands were carved up among the three cities', held jointly. The page gives no boundary; the Federal District stands for the western shore.

region.text: Coyoacan in the Basin of Mexico

ledger.note: 1429: Coyoacan, first target of the new empire. 'The first targets for imperial expansion were Coyoacan in the Basin of Mexico' after the Tepanec defeat; the Itzcoatl page mentions its conquest (with Culhuacan) without a year, so 1429 is a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Xochimilco, on the southern lake

ledger.note: 1430: Itzcoatl takes Xochimilco. 'Successful campaigns against Xochimilco (1430), Mixquic (1432), Cuitlahuac (1433)'. The place name is not in the gazetteer (a 12 km disc is my reading).

region.text: Mixquic

ledger.note: 1432: Mixquic falls to Itzcoatl (Itzcoatl page, same sentence).

region.text: Cuitlahuac (Tlahuac)

ledger.note: 1433: Cuitlahuac falls to Itzcoatl (Itzcoatl page, same sentence).

region.text: Cuauhnahuac (Cuernavaca) and Huaxtepec in the state of Morelos

ledger.note: 1439: Itzcoatl's campaign takes Cuauhnahuac and opens Morelos. 'In 1439, Itzcoatl undertook a campaign outside the Valley of Mexico against Cuauhnahuac (Cuernavaca)'; the Aztec page lists Cuauhnahuac and Huaxtepec among 'the first targets'. The page does not say the campaign succeeded in 1439; the 1440 shape has Morelos.

region.text: Hidalgo, eastern Puebla and the first Gulf cells: 'expand the empire east towards the Gulf of Mexico'

ledger.note: 1450: the empire reaches east over Hidalgo and Puebla. The Moctezuma I page ('1440-1469') says he extended 'the boundaries of the Aztec empire beyond the Valley of Mexico to the Gulf Coast' and 'maintain[ed] peace from 1440 to 1453 within his empire'; it dates no conquest here, so the year is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1). The drought of 1450-1454 and the later re-conquest of 'several cities in Morelos' (Aztec page) are not dated further.

region.text: the Gulf Coast of Veracruz: 'subjugating the Huastec people and Totonac peoples'

ledger.note: 1453: the Gulf Coast comes under the Aztecs. 'subjugating the Huastec people and Totonac peoples' (Moctezuma I page, no year); the year is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1).

region.text: Cempoala, the Totonac strategic province

ledger.note: 1453: the Totonac city of Cempoala becomes a client of the alliance. The Aztec page lists Cempoala as a 'strategic' province, 'essentially subordinate client states which provided tribute or aid' (its prose also calls it a tributary province); no year is given, so the date is that of the Gulf Coast gain (confidence 1).

region.text: the Toluca Valley, 'claiming lands previously conquered by Motecuzoma and Itzcoatl'

ledger.note: 1455: the Tarascans invade the Toluca Valley. 'In 1455, the Purepecha under their king Tzitzipandaquare had invaded the Toluca Valley, claiming lands previously conquered by Motecuzoma and Itzcoatl.' The Tarascan page puts the Tarascan advance into the Toluca Valley in 1460. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: Toluca disc cut from 60 to 50 km: at 60 km it reached the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan)]

region.text: Mixtec territory: the city-state of Coixtlahuaca

ledger.note: 1458: Moctezuma I marches on the Mixtec city-state of Coixtlahuaca. 'In about 1458, Moctezuma led an expedition into Mixtec territory against the city-state of Coixtlahuaca.' The page does not state the outcome; the Aztec page lists Coixtlahuaca as a tributary province. The same page has 'he conquered the state of Oaxaca in 1445' and 'In the 1450s, Aztec forces under Moctezuma would invade the Valley of Oaxaca' (the Aztec page puts the Oaxaca Valley in 1486).

region.text: the Valley of Oaxaca: 'In the 1450s, Aztec forces under Moctezuma would invade the Valley of Oaxaca'

ledger.note: 1459: the Valley of Oaxaca is added to the shape. The page's '1450s' invasion is fitted to Cliopatria's 1459 shape (42 Oaxaca cells); the Aztec page attributes the Oaxaca Valley to Ahuitzotl's wave from 1486.

region.text: northern Guerrero, including the tributary province of Tlapan

ledger.note: 1459: Guerrero is added to the shape. The Aztec page lists Tlapan among the tributary provinces and gives no year; the year is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1).

region.text: the Toluca Valley

ledger.note: 1472: Axayacatl holds the Toluca Valley. 'In 1472, Axayacatl re-conquered the region and successfully defended it from Purepecha's attempts to take it back.' The Axayacatl page has the Matlatzinca of the Toluca Valley in 1474. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: Toluca disc cut from 60 to 50 km: at 60 km it reached the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan)]

region.text: the Toluca Valley, re-conquered; the Axayacatl page says 'the Matlatzinca of the Toluca Valley in 1474'

ledger.note: 1472: the Toluca Valley returns to the alliance (the shape shows it from 1475).

region.text: Tlatelolco, Tenochtitlan's 'sister city'

ledger.note: 1473: Axayacatl takes Tlatelolco. 'he led successful campaigns against the neighboring altepetl of Tlatelolco in 1473'; the Tenochtitlan page has 'the war of Tenochtitlan against its neighbor Tlatelolco in 1473'. The altepetl lay beside Tenochtitlan, so the shape does not change.

region.text: frontier towns on the Tarascan border: 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns'

ledger.note: 1475: Axayacatl's frontier towns on the Tarascan border. 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns' (Tarascan state page, no year); the six Michoacan cells in Cliopatria's shape appear in 1475, which is the year used (page silent on the year, confidence 1). The Tarascans later 'repelled the attacks'.

region.text: the Aztec-Tarascan frontier in eastern Michoacan and the Toluca Valley

ledger.note: 1476: Axayacatl is defeated by the Tarascans and the frontier stays disputed. Axayacatl was 'finally defeated by the Tarascans of Michoacan in 1476'; the Tarascan page has 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns' and 'From 1480 the Aztec ruler Ahuitzotl intensified the conflict'; the Aztec page has a failed invasion of 32,000 men in 1479.

region.text: the conquests of Tizoc's reign: about fourteen altepetl including Ecatepec, Tlappan and Mazatlan (Codex Mendoza)

ledger.note: 1482: Tizoc's conquests extend the shape over Puebla, Veracruz and Hidalgo. The Tizoc page credits him with about fourteen altepetl and a Matlatzinca rebellion put down, with no years; the year is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1). The shape's growth includes Tlaxcala (corrected in the keyframes).

region.text: the Oaxaca Valley

ledger.note: 1486: Ahuitzotl begins a new wave of conquests. 'Ahuitzotl then began a new wave of conquests including the Oaxaca Valley and the Soconusco Coast.' The Ahuitzotl page: 'He conquered the Mixtec, Zapotec, and other peoples from Pacific Coast of Mexico down to the western part of Guatemala.' [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: confidence 2 to 1: the pages date Ahuitzotl's accession (1486), not the conquest of the Oaxaca Valley]

region.text: the Soconusco Coast (Xoconochco), 'an Aztec exclave near the present-day Guatemalan border'

ledger.note: 1486: the Soconusco Coast is taken in Ahuitzotl's wave (the Cliopatria shape shows it from 1492). The Aztec page lists Xoconochco among the tributary provinces. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: was 1486 at confidence 2; the Aztec Empire and Ahuitzotl pages give no year for the Soconusco conquest (only Ahuitzotl's reign, 1486-1502), and the 1487 keyframe does not hold Soconusco, so the year is Cliopatria's 1492 shape (page silent, confidence 1)]

region.text: the Pacific Coast of Guerrero

ledger.note: 1497: the Pacific Coast of Guerrero. 'Ahuitzotl conquered the border city of Otzoma, and he expanded to the Pacific Coast of Guerrero' (Aztec page, no year within 1486-1502); the year is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1).

region.text: Achiotlan and the Mixtec lands of Oaxaca

ledger.note: 1504: Moctezuma II's first important conquest. 'The first important conquest during Moctezuma's rule occurred in the year 1504' (Achiotlan); Zozollan followed on 28 May 1506 'during the campaign against the Yanhuitlan rebellion' and Tototepec about 1507. Cliopatria shows the whole 1502 increment from 1502.

region.text: the Aztec-Tarascan frontier

ledger.note: 1515: the last Aztec invasion of the Tarascan state fails. 'In 1515, Aztec armies commanded by the Tlaxcalan general Tlahuicole invaded the Purepecha Empire once again'; the army 'failed to take any territory'. The frontier is the same until the Spanish conquest.

region.text: Cempoala and the Totonac chiefs

ledger.note: 1519: the Totonacs rebel with Cortes. 'Cortes quickly persuaded the Totonac chiefs to rebel against the Aztecs' (early 1519, no day given).

region.text: Tenochtitlan

ledger.note: 8 November 1519: Cortes enters Tenochtitlan. 'On 8 November 1519, after the fall of Cholula, Cortes and his forces entered' the city; 'As of 14 November 1519, Moctezuma was Cortes' prisoner'. The Spaniards are guests turned jailers, not sovereigns, so the city is drawn hatched.

region.text: Tenochtitlan

ledger.note: June 1520: the Spaniards are driven out on the Noche Triste. The conquest page's timeline has 30 June 1520 ('Evacuation of Spanish-Tlaxcalteca allied forces from Tenochtitlan'); its narrative says 'the rainy night of 10 July 1520'; Moctezuma II died on 29 June 1520 (his page). Month 6 follows the timeline and the Moctezuma II page.

region.text: the Valley of Mexico and the Puebla basin: Tepeaca was punished in August 1520

ledger.note: August 1520: the Spaniards and their Tlaxcalan allies strike back from Tlaxcala. 'Tepeaca was punished in August 1520 for killing Spaniards', and the siege of Tenochtitlan began on 10 May 1521. The contest runs to the fall of the capital.

region.text: Texcoco, which 'had already become firm allies of the Spaniards'

ledger.note: February 1521: Texcoco turns against Tenochtitlan. 'Texcoco becomes the base of operations for the campaign against Tenochtitlan' (timeline, February 1521); the Aztec page says Texcoco 'had already become firm allies of the Spaniards'. Tlacopan and Xaltocan were attacked the same month. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region was Cliopatria's Texcoco 1428 shape, which the texcoco dossier finds lies south of the lake (Xochimilco, Chalco); now the corrected Texcoco disc]

region.text: the Valley of Mexico and the Puebla basin

ledger.note: 13 August 1521: Tenochtitlan surrenders. 'Surrender of Aztec defenders; capture of Cuauhtemoc' after a siege that began on 10 May 1521.

region.text: the Triple Alliance's whole shape

ledger.note: 13 August 1521: the empire falls to the Spaniards. 'the empire fell into Spanish control on 13 August 1521'; infobox 'Spanish conquest: 13 August 1521'. Cuauhtemoc was kept prisoner and executed in 1525 with the other rulers of the former Triple Alliance.

region.text: the Triple Alliance and its tributary provinces

ledger.note: 13 August 1521: the Aztec Triple Alliance ends. 'defeated them in 1521'; infobox 'Spanish conquest: 13 August 1521'. The land passes to the Spanish Empire (identity.successors); Tlaxcala, Cempoala and Texcoco had already joined the Spaniards.

wars.name: Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Azcapotzalco defeated in 1428; the Tepanec lands carved up among Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, who formed the Triple Alliance (the treaty in 1430). Huexotzinco withdrew.
wars.note: Tezozomoc died in 1426; Maxtla usurped the throne from Tayahauh and Chimalpopoca of Tenochtitlan died shortly after, 'possibly assassinated by Maxtla'; Nezahualcoyotl 'fled into exile' and recruited help from Huexotzinco. The page names no siege or battle; the contest is carried by the predecessors' dossiers.

wars.name: Conquest of the lake cities and Morelos
wars.outcome: Xochimilco (1430), Mixquic (1432), Cuitlahuac (1433) and Cuauhnahuac (campaign of 1439) taken by Itzcoatl.
wars.note: Coyoacan and Culhuacan are named without years.

wars.name: Flower wars with Tlaxcala
wars.outcome: Ritual wars 'mostly waged between the Aztec Empire and the neighboring cities of their arch-enemy Tlaxcala'; Tlaxcala was never taken and allied with Cortes on 23 September 1519.
wars.note: The Moctezuma II page has the first large-scale conflicts with Tlaxcala about 1504 or 1505 and Huejotzingo leaving the empire's alliance about 1516. The flower wars take no ground, so no contest is drawn.

wars.name: Aztec-Tarascan wars
wars.outcome: The Tarascans invaded the Toluca Valley in 1455 and were driven out in 1472; they defeated Axayacatl in 1476 and again in 1479 ('a resounding victory' over 32,000 men); an Aztec invasion in 1515 under Tlahuicole 'failed to take any territory'. The Tarascan state was never conquered.
wars.note: Fortified frontier posts such as Cutzamala are named on the Tarascan page (undated).

wars.name: Conquest of Tlatelolco
wars.outcome: Axayacatl's campaigns against the neighbouring altepetl of Tlatelolco in 1473 ended its independence; the Tenochtitlan page calls it Tenochtitlan's sister city.

wars.name: Mixtec and Oaxaca campaigns
wars.outcome: Expedition against Coixtlahuaca about 1458; the Oaxaca Valley and Soconusco from 1486; Achiotlan in 1504 and Zozollan (Yanhuitlan rebellion) on 28 May 1506.
wars.note: The Moctezuma I page: 'In about 1458, Moctezuma led an expedition into Mixtec territory against the city-state of Coixtlahuaca'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

zones.text: Tepeaca, Cholula and the road from Tlaxcala

wars.outcome: Cortes landed on 21-22 April 1519, allied with the Totonacs of Cempoala and, on 23 September 1519, with Tlaxcala; he entered Tenochtitlan on 8 November 1519, was driven out on the Noche Triste (30 June or 10 July 1520, the page gives both) and besieged the city from 10 May 1521 until its surrender on 13 August 1521.
wars.note: Cholula's massacre was in October 1519; Cholula had seceded from the Tlaxcalan alliance in 1517 to become an Aztec tributary.

certainty.note: A hegemonic, 'territorially discontinuous' empire ('Aztec rule has been described as hegemonic or indirect'); no border was surveyed or fixed by treaty, and the enclaves (Tlaxcala, Huexotzinco, Cholula, the Tarascan frontier) are only approximate. The Tarascan frontier was the one stable line after 1479 but is still drawn soft.

sources.title: Aztec Empire
sources.note: Identity, 1428 foundation, 1430 treaty, 220,000 km2 for 1520, provinces, Tarascan wars, Tlaxcala, Cempoala, 38 tributary provinces.

sources.title: Tepanec War (redirects to Aztec Empire)
sources.note: The request redirected to the Aztec Empire article (title 'Triple Alliance Excan Tlahtoloyan'): 1426 death of Tezozomoc, Maxtla, 1427-1428 war, 1430 treaty, Tepanec lands carved up.

sources.title: Moctezuma I
sources.note: Reign 1440-1469; peace 1440-1453; drought 1450; Oaxaca 1445, Coixtlahuaca about 1458; Gulf Coast, Huastec and Totonac undated.

sources.title: Axayacatl
sources.note: Reign 1469-1481; Tlatelolco 1473; Toluca Valley 1474; defeat by the Tarascans 1476.

sources.title: Tizoc
sources.note: Reign 1481-1486; about fourteen altepetl (Codex Mendoza), no years.

sources.title: Ahuitzotl
sources.note: Reign 1486-1502; conquests of the Mixtec and Zapotec down to Guatemala (no years); Templo Mayor 1487.

sources.title: Moctezuma II
sources.note: Reign 1502/1503-1520; Achiotlan 1504, Zozollan 1506, Tlaxcala conflicts, Huejotzingo 1516, Cortes 1519, death June 1520.

sources.title: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
sources.note: Dated sequence 1519-1521: Totonac revolt, Tlaxcala 23 September 1519, Tenochtitlan 8 November 1519, Noche Triste, siege from 10 May 1521, fall 13 August 1521.

sources.title: Tarascan state
sources.note: Tarascan frontier: 1460 expansion, 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns', from 1480 Ahuitzotl, 75,000 km2 for 1450.

sources.title: Tenochtitlan
sources.note: Infobox 'Formation of the Aztec Empire: 1428'; Tlatelolco 1473; city size.

sources.title: Acolhua
sources.note: Alliance 'founded in 1428'; Texcoco as an eastern-Basin kingdom.

sources.title: Metztitlán
sources.note: 'unconquered by the Aztec Empire'; a powerful, independent Otomi state in Hidalgo; no founding date or boundary.

notes: Pages: Aztec Empire (twice, different questions, and via the Tepanec War redirect), the reign pages of Itzcoatl, Moctezuma I, Axayacatl, Tizoc, Ahuitzotl and Moctezuma II, the Spanish conquest, the Tarascan state, Tenochtitlan, Acolhua and Metztitlan: twelve articles against a budget of five, spent because the shape changes at 1450, 1453, 1459, 1475, 1482, 1487, 1492, 1497 and 1502 can only be matched to reigns on those pages. (1) START: the pages put the foundation in 1428 (infobox; the Tepanec War victory), the treaty in 1430; Cliopatria starts in 1429. The dossier starts in 1428 with a one-year keyframe; Tenochtitlan and Texcoco end the same year. (2) END: 13 August 1521, not 1520; Cliopatria's Spanish Empire starts 1521 on the same land. (3) TLAXCALA AND METZTITLAN: Cliopatria's shape contains all of Tlaxcala by 1482 and Metztitlan from 1450; every shape from 1450 is corrected by removing both; Huejotzingo and Cholula are also inside the Puebla cells and are independent or allied at times (Huejotzingo left the alliance in about 1516, Cholula became a tributary in 1517 after leaving the Tlaxcalan alliance) but the pages do not give their status year by year, so they are left in. Metztitlan (an independent Otomi state in Hidalgo, 'unconquered by the Aztec Empire', Metztitlan page) is cut out of every shape from 1450 with a 30 km disc round the town (the page gives no boundary; the town's coordinates are not from a page); the Yopi (Yopitzingo) in Guerrero are not on any page read. (4) THE SHAPE CHANGES 1450-1453, 1459, 1482, 1487, 1492-1502 are mostly undated in the pages: ledger events at confidence 1 use the Cliopatria shape-differences as regions. (5) CONFLICTS between pages: Oaxaca 1445 (Moctezuma I page) vs Valley of Oaxaca 1450s vs Ahuitzotl 1486 (Aztec page); Toluca Valley 1472 (Aztec page) vs 1474 (Axayacatl page); the Tarascan defeat 1476 (Axayacatl page) vs 1479 (Aztec page); Noche Triste 30 June or 10 July 1520 (conquest page); Triple Alliance 1428 (infobox) vs 1430 (treaty). (6) THE TARASCAN FRONTIER: Cliopatria's shape has six Michoacan and nine Guanajuato cells inside the Aztec shape from 1475; the Tarascan state was never conquered. (7) The vassal tint is used for Cempoala only, the one client (strategic) province the pages name; the 38 tributary provinces were run by stewards (huecalpixque) and are drawn as part of the empire. (8) The summarising tool behind the page fetches gave the quoted sentences; where a sentence is in single quotes it is the page's wording as returned. (9) Gazetteer names needed: Xochimilco, Mixquic, Cuitlahuac, Cempoala, Coixtlahuaca, Metztitlan. (10) Counterparts without a dossier: Tlacopan, Coyoacan, Xochimilco, Mixquic, Cuitlahuac, Cuauhnahuac, Tlatelolco, Coixtlahuaca, Cempoala (Totonacs), the Mixtec and Zapotec polities, Huexotzinco, Cholula (dossier cholula exists, another group), Metztitlan (no dated page).
